# Security Checklist: ISK-0009 — Module Events & Background Work Coordination

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements for scope isolation at every worker, job, and directory boundary, the scope directory's policies and race, the directory row's attestation, and value-free telemetry are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and measurable, for Security owner review before `implement`
**Created**: 2026-11-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Scope isolation

- [x] CHK001 - Is it stated, for every item read and write, which scope's unit performs it, including operator-scope items? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, Contract §Scopes and the directory 1, §The outbox 4]
- [x] CHK002 - Is FR-009's rule, as decided in `plan`, stated the same way in every place the spec describes the operator unit's reach, including the user stories' independent tests? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §US4]
  - Settled in `checklist`: US4's independent test said an operator-scope unit reads no item, contrary to the `plan` decision that operator-scope items exist. It now says no tenant item.
- [x] CHK003 - Is the scope of each job's reads and writes stated, so that no job reads or deletes a tenant row in an operator unit? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020, §FR-021, Contract §Recurring jobs 4, 5]
- [x] CHK004 - Is the enqueue scope check defined against the unit's own scope, with the failure before any write? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §US4.2, Contract §The outbox 2]
- [x] CHK005 - Can the isolation requirements be measured independently of repository predicates, as SC-005's "with the predicate removed" requires? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005, Tasks T036, T037]

## Scope directory

- [x] CHK006 - Are the directory's policies stated per command, with the operator's read exception and the limit of every write to the unit's own row? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, Persistence §Isolation 9, Research R2]
- [x] CHK007 - Is the directory's content limited to the canonical scope, a module name, and a due time, and is what it reveals to an operator stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §Assumptions, Contract §Scopes and the directory 3]
- [x] CHK008 - Is the register and settle protocol defined precisely enough to show that no committed item or expiring row is left without its row, at every producer isolation level? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, Persistence §Isolation 10, Research R3]
- [x] CHK009 - Does SC-005's removal race cover both modules that register rows, the outbox's items and the coordinator's expiring rows, with a task for each? [Coverage, Spec §SC-005, §FR-007, Tasks T038, T040]
  - Settled in `checklist`: T038 raced only the outbox's producers. T040 now adds `SettleDirectoryRaceTests`, the same race for the `coordination` module against coordinator inserts. It sits in T040 rather than T038 because `SettleDirectoryAsync` arrives in Phase 7.
- [x] CHK010 - Is it stated which writes of the PostgreSQL coordinator register a scope, and why an update needs no registration? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, Coordination §Atomic operations 7, Research R3]
- [x] CHK011 - Is the absence of any function or role that bypasses row-level security stated as a requirement, with how AV-1 is validated? [Assumption, Spec §AV-1, Plan §Constraints, Research R2]

## Directory row attestation

- [x] CHK012 - Are the accepted canonical forms of a directory row stated exactly, with the rule that an ID's canonical text must equal the input? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, Contract §Scopes and the directory 4, Research R4]
- [x] CHK013 - Is the handling of a malformed row defined, including that it is never widened to operator or another scope, and that its event carries no scope? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, §US4.4, Contract §Diagnostics 8009]
- [x] CHK014 - Is it stated that only the dispatcher and the jobs may turn a stored scope into a unit scope, and through which ISK-0002 seam? [Clarity, Spec §TR-5, Research R4]

## Fencing and exclusion

- [x] CHK015 - Is it stated that the fencing guard accepts only PostgreSQL-issued leases, and how a worker without them is refused before it runs anything? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, §US2.5, Coordination §Leases and fencing 6]
- [x] CHK016 - Is the ban on advisory locks as leases, fences, or mutual exclusion stated, and can it be checked mechanically? [Measurability, Spec §FR-024, Tasks T032]

## Telemetry and payloads

- [x] CHK017 - Is the telemetry vocabulary closed, listing every allowed field and label, and every value that may never appear? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033, §FR-034, Contract §Diagnostics]
- [x] CHK018 - Is the payload's content restricted (no secret, credential, prompt, or response text), and is it excluded from every log, trace, metric, error, and readiness answer? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, Contract §Work items 2]
- [x] CHK019 - Is the use of stored trace context limited to the dispatch link, with untrusted outside context bounded in size? [Clarity, Spec §TR-15, Contract §Tracing 1, 4]
- [x] CHK020 - Is SC-008's canary defined over every outcome that writes telemetry, so "0 identifiers" is measurable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008, Tasks T055]

## Review and threat model

- [x] CHK021 - Does every threat in the Negative Security and Failure Scenarios table map to a requirement and a contract rule? [Traceability, Spec §Negative Security and Failure Scenarios, Contract §Threat model]
- [x] CHK022 - Are the sections that need Security owner review named in the contracts? [Completeness, Spec §TR-4, Contract header, Persistence and Coordination change tables]
- [x] CHK023 - Is the worker's database login stated, so that the long-running worker holds no migration login? [Gap, Local environment §Documents 2, Container §Start-up 5]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
